Definition: from G4687; a scattering (of seed), i.e. (concretely) seed (as sown):--seed (X sown).
BiblicalUsage: The seed as sown is the subject of the parable. A sower went out to sow his seed, and the parable is this: the seed is the word of God, and the kingdom is as if a man should cast seed into the ground.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the seed is the word, and the ground is the heart, and the harvest depends on which ground the word finds.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
